skills.name: Accounting for trading transactions: purchases and sales

note.text:
Trading transactions are the buying and selling of goods.
• Purchase on credit: debit 601 Purchases of goods (HT), debit 445 VAT recoverable, credit 401 Suppliers (TTC).
• Sale on credit: debit 411 Customers (TTC), credit 701 Sales of goods (HT), credit 443 VAT invoiced.
• Cash sale or purchase: use 571 Cash (or 521 Bank) instead of 411 or 401.
• Trade discount (rabais, remise): a reduction on the invoice; VAT is calculated on the net amount after discount.

sections.heading: Buying goods
sections.text:
Goods bought for resale go to {'601 Purchases of goods'} (amount excluding tax). The VAT paid goes to {'445 VAT recoverable'}.
If bought on credit, the supplier is owed the total: credit {'401 Suppliers'} with the amount including tax. If paid at once, credit {'571 Cash'} or {'521 Bank'}.

sections.heading: Selling goods
sections.text:
Sales of goods are income: credit {'701 Sales of goods'} with the amount excluding tax and {'443 VAT invoiced'} with the VAT.
On credit, debit {'411 Customers'} with the total including tax; for cash, debit {'571 Cash'}.
A sale of {200000} FCFA HT: {'Dr 411'} {238500}, {'Cr 701'} {200000}, {'Cr 443'} {38500}.

sections.heading: Trade discounts
sections.text:
A trade discount (rabais, remise) reduces the price on the invoice, for example for a regular customer or a large order.
Work out the net amount first: list price − discount. Then calculate VAT on the net amount.
{200000} FCFA less {10}%: net {180000}, VAT {34650}, total {214650} FCFA.

key_words.meaning: a price reduction shown on the invoice

mistake.wrong: VAT is calculated on the list price before the discount
mistake.right: VAT is calculated on the net price after the discount
mistake.why: Tax is charged only on what the customer actually pays for the goods.

worked_example.problem: Goods listed at {g} FCFA are sold on credit with a {d}% trade discount (VAT {19.25}%). Find the net, the VAT and the total the customer owes.
steps: TTC = {g * (100 - d) / 100 * 1.1925} FCFA, debited to {'411 Customers'}.

cards.idea: Purchases: debit Purchases and VAT recoverable; credit Suppliers.
Sales: debit Customers; credit Sales and VAT invoiced.
VAT is calculated after any trade discount.

check.prompt: Goods listed at {g} FCFA are sold with a {d}% trade discount. What is the net amount excluding tax (FCFA)?

misconceptions.explain: That is the discount; subtract it from the list price.

pick.q: Goods are bought on credit for 100 000 FCFA HT (VAT 19 250).
pick.r: Dr 601 Purchases 100 000; Dr 445 VAT recoverable 19 250 / Cr 401 Suppliers 119 250
e: It is on credit, and the VAT is recorded separately.
pick.y: Purchases and recoverable VAT debited; the supplier credited TTC.

pick.q: Goods are sold on credit for 200 000 FCFA HT (VAT 38 500).
pick.r: Dr 411 Customers 238 500 / Cr 701 Sales 200 000; Cr 443 VAT invoiced 38 500
e: It is a credit sale, and VAT must be shown separately.
pick.y: The customer owes the TTC amount.

pick.q: Goods are sold for cash: 50 000 FCFA HT (VAT 9 625).
pick.r: Dr 571 Cash 59 625 / Cr 701 Sales 50 000; Cr 443 VAT invoiced 9 625
e: It is a cash sale, not on credit.
The VAT collected must be recorded.
pick.y: Cash comes in for the full TTC.

questions.prompt: Goods are bought on credit for {ht} FCFA HT (VAT {19.25}%). What amount is credited to {'401'} Suppliers (FCFA)?

misconceptions.explain: The supplier is owed the amount including VAT.

questions.prompt: Goods listed at {g} FCFA are sold with a {d}% trade discount. What is the net amount excluding tax (FCFA)?

misconceptions.explain: That is the discount; subtract it from the list price.

questions.prompt: Goods listed at {g} FCFA are sold on credit with a {d}% trade discount (VAT {19.25}%). What amount is debited to {'411'} Customers (FCFA)?

misconceptions.explain: Apply the discount first, then add VAT on the net amount.
